newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan calls on G7 to resolve Peru hostage drama.
newsitem.headline: Japan calls on G7 to resolve Peru hostage drama.

text.p: Japan has asked fellow members of the Group of Seven (G7) industrialised nations to hammer out a joint solution to the 10-day-old Peru hostage crisis, Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda said on Friday.
Ikeda told a news conference Japan had begun consultations with fellow G7 members Britain, Germany, France, Italy, Canada, and the United States to draft a joint plan to end the drama.
Japan's surprise move to seek a G7 solution to the crisis followed a similar proposal from Russian President Boris Yeltsin earlier in the week.
In his proposal, Ikeda referred to appeals Yeltsin made in letters to G7 leaders and to Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori to adopt a collective G7 approach to the hostage crisis.

In the letters, Yeltsin suggested a joint declaration by the G7 plus Russia offering coordinated moves to resolve the crisis, including the possible dispatch of anti-terrorist squads and establishment of a joint headquarters to conduct a hostage-freeing operation in Lima.
Peruvian Marxist guerrillas are holding more than 100 hostages inside the Lima residence of the Japanese ambassador to Peru after storming into the compound during a packed reception on December 17.

"It is clear that the international community should not condone terrorism. It is also necessary for the international community to act as one to help resolve this crisis by setting free all the hostages peacefully, and at an early date," Ikeda said.
"With this in mind, we have already started consultations (with the other G7 member states)."
At the summit of G7 leaders in Lyon, France, last July, the world's seven most industrialised nations approved a list of 25 practical measures to defeat terrorism.

The package included pledges to reinforce police cooperation and training, to share intelligence, make extradition procedures easier, cut off sources of terrorist funding and weapons, and strengthen national anti-terrorism legislation.
